definitions.explanation: People who share a common purpose or interest and voluntarily come together for a cause or activity. Implies willing participation rather than obligation.

examples.japanese: {有志|ゆうし}を{募|つの}ってイベントを{企画|きかく}した。
examples.english: We recruited volunteers and planned an event.

examples.japanese: {社員|しゃいん}の{有志|ゆうし}が{清掃|せいそう}{活動|かつどう}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: Volunteer employees carried out a cleanup activity.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{有志|ゆうし}が{集|あつ}まって、{子|こ}どもたちのための{学習|がくしゅう}{支援|しえん}プログラムを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: Local volunteers came together and launched a learning support program for children.

notes:
USAGE:
Used to describe people who voluntarily participate in something. Often appears in the pattern {有志|ゆうし}を{募|つの}る (to recruit volunteers) or {有志|ゆうし}による (by volunteers). More formal than ボランティア and emphasizes shared purpose rather than unpaid labor.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有志|ゆうし}を{募|つの}る: to recruit volunteers
- {有志|ゆうし}による: by volunteers, volunteer-run
- {有志|ゆうし}が{集|あつ}まる: volunteers gather
- {有志|ゆうし}の{会|かい}: a group of interested parties

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ボランティア: volunteer (loanword, broader)
- {志願者|しがんしゃ}: volunteer, applicant (formal)
